newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil sellers hunt buyers, spreads stable.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil sellers hunt buyers, spreads stable.

text.p: European gas oil trade was virtually bereft of buying interest on Tuesday with hot weather and holidays continuing to drain momentum from business, traders said.
Outright prices firmed around $2 a tonne. Front month September IPE gained $2.25 a tonne, boosted by stronger Brent to settle at the day's high of $171.75.
A cargo of low sulphur EN590 diesel continued to be rumoured sold to a British major at around September +$4.75 cif NWE on a private and confidential basis.

German heating oil suffered from a lack of buying interest from Germany, the continent's main winter heating oil market. Heating oil was September +$0.50/+$0.75 for September 1-10. Differentials for late August were discussed sporadically at September +$0.75 offered but no bid was heard.
The barge market was equally unresponsive. Low sulphur diesel was at premiums of +$4.75/$5.00 for storage at $5.50 for refinery.
Rotterdam refinery heating oil into the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp region was at September IPE flat for August. September delivery was discussed at a premium of $1 to September IPE.
